Computes the bounding box in Normalized Device Coordinates (NDC) space from a set of rays.
- **Time Complexity:** $O(N \cdot S)$, where $N$ is the number of rays and $S$ is the average number of samples per ray.
The intersection calculation is $O(N)$, and point generation is $O(N \cdot S)$.

- **Strengths:** Ensures samples are only generated within the valid scene volume, reducing unnecessary computations for empty space.
Handles edge cases like zero-direction rays and near-far clipping robustly.
- **When to Use:** When rendering volumetric data within a known bounding box, especially in coarse geometry search phases or when using fixed-step ray marching.
- **When Not to Use:** When the scene geometry is highly irregular and a tight bounding box is not available, or when adaptive step sizes are required for high-frequency details.
This method is a core component of differentiable volume rendering pipelines, particularly those based on Direct Volume Rendering (DVR) or Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) with explicit bounding boxes.
